Destinations · Issue 14

Six Islands Worth the Long Way Round

Quiet anchorages, a bakery that opens at dawn, and the best sunset on the whole sound.

PC
Priya Castellan10 November 2026 · 11 min read

The outer islands reward the people who make the effort, and punish the ones who hurry. Here are six worth the long way round, in the order we would visit them.

Little Holm has one house, one beach, and the best anchorage on the sound in a westerly. Skerry Holm has the bakery, the ferry and the light. Fair Isle of Avelin has a ruined chapel and a colony of puffins from May to July. The Shearwaters are three rocks and a lot of birds; anchor off and listen at dusk. Morrow has a pub with a fire. Inis Calla has nothing at all, which is the point.

Bring a good anchor, a tide table and more bread than you think you need. The islands will take care of the rest. ■
